data.description:
## Context
Repository delegation must not blur the boundary between local multi-file persistence and the existing selective tickets-branch publication seam. The ownership and partial-state rules need durable documentation and regression guards.

## Outcome
Finalize the S1 cutover with ADR 0099 and cross-seam tests proving the existing five-file allowlist, unchanged-pass behavior, rotation floor, and retired-first publication semantics remain intact.

## Plan
1. Add failing regressions around selective commit staging, unchanged passes, GET rotation, and retired-state publication.
2. Keep publication in `reconcile_helpers.py`; do not publish each repository checkpoint or broaden staging.
3. Record repository versus publication ownership, ordered partial-state behavior, rollback, and no-journal/no-format-migration decisions in ADR 0099 and its index.
4. Run the full binding-state regression set after removing superseded facade persistence branches.

## Testing
Use existing held-out selective-publication suites plus ADR index checks. Assert repository failures do not cause unrelated tracker staging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tickets publication stages only the existing five bridge-state files.
- [ ] An unchanged pass creates no commit.
- [ ] GET rotation and retired-first failure cases preserve the pre-extraction publication and recovery floors.
- [ ] Repository checkpoints never publish independently.
- [ ] ADR 0099 records ownership, ordered partial states, selective publication, rollback, and explicit no-journal/no-format-migration decisions.

## Out of scope
Lifecycle extraction and new interrupted-retirement recovery remain S2/S3.
data.title: RP-02 S1 T3 — Lock persistence ownership and selective publication
